newsitem.title: USA: 75pct of MIA international air cargo on freighters.
newsitem.headline: 75pct of MIA international air cargo on freighters.

text.p: About three-quarters of international air cargo passing through Miami International Airport (MIA) moves in freighters and that is expected to increase, a top MIA official told a conference here Wednesday.

"This year about 75 percent of the international cargo will be carried on freighters and next year that will be 80 percent," Peter Reaveley, manager of route development told the Miami Conference on the Caribbean and Latin America.

"This could go to 85 percent by the year 2000," Reaveley said. Volumes of cargo are increasing rapidly, while at the same time the passenger planes are fuller and have less space for cargo, he explained.

Reaveley expects continued strong growth in Latin American cargo. "We expect gross domestic product rates in South America to grow four to six percent (annually) over the next ten years. The normal rule of thumb is to multiply that by 2.5 to get cargo growth rates," he said.
But in Latin America he predicts cargo will grow at three times GDP or about 15 percent, "and remember at 15 percent, you are doubling your base number every five years."
He attributes the higher multiple to strong growth in perishables and the need to rebuild infrastructure and add factories in Latin America.

MIA is unquestionably the hub for Latin American perishables. MIA received 40 tons of fresh fish from Chile every morning, 40 tons of fresh raspberries from Chile every morning and far more than that in flowers from Latin America every day, he said. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
